newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan opposes S.Korea's bicycle tariff plan.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan opposes S.Korea's bicycle tariff plan.

text.p: Taiwan on Tuesday urged talks with South Korea in a bid to dissuade Seoul from slapping emergency tariffs on imports of Taiwan-made bicycles and parts.

Taiwan's economics ministry said South Korea's trade commission on February 27 suggested an emergency 21.7 percent tariff on top of a basic eight percent tariff on imports of bicycles and parts from Taiwan.
The tariff also would affect imports from China, where Taiwan-financed bicycle factories are major exporters.
Seoul was expected to take a decision within 45 days of receiving the recommendation, which was seen in Taipei as being politically motivated.

Taipei's United Daily News on Tuesday said Seoul was retaliating for Taiwan's controversial plan to ship low-level nuclear waste for storage in Stalinist North Korea -- South Korea's mercurial adversary.

The ministry complained that Seoul should negotiate with Taipei before taking such an action under a December 1996 agreement to conduct trade based on World Trade Organisation regulations and principles.
"According to WTO rules, Korea should launch talks with our country before taking defensive moves," the statement said.

Pyongyang agreed in January to accept up to 200,000 barrels of contaminated clothing and other refuse discarded by the state-run Taiwan Power Co's three nuclear power plants in a deal reported to be worth US$1,150 per barrel or US$230 million.
South Korea has sought international support to stop the shipment, citing potential environmental and health hazards it would introduce to the Korean peninsula.
Taiwan maintains the waste deal is in line with international safeguards and poses no danger.
